gen-gf-baumans-general-sans: General Sans reads smooth and steady, its x-height filling the line. What stands out is how Baumans, with its wrench-wide c and uniform strokes, sits beside a body that stands noticeably taller in the lowercase.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-orbit: Blunt and distinctive, with a crescent-wrench c and uniform strokes, Baumans stands out. And Baumans earns its place in big, brief lines, while Orbit's sans-serif text floats its characters apart with curves that stop short of closing.
gen-gf-baumans-gf-science-gothic: Baumans arrives with a crescent-wrench c and strokes of uniform width. Science Gothic, a sans-serif with wide-set stroke ends and no swelling or thinning, shares that single line width, which is what ties the two together.
gen-gf-baumans-manrope: Distinctive at a glance, Baumans brings a crescent-wrench c and uniform strokes. Yet the heading's worth shows big and short, while Manrope leaves a bright gap at the mouth of every curve.
gen-gf-baumans-montserrat: Montserrat gives every curve lots of white space leading in. Bump its size up a notch and the oversized e and a counters glide like wire beneath Baumans and its crescent-wrench c.
gen-gf-baumans-satoshi: A crescent-wrench c, opened wide, marks Baumans, a display face whose every stroke holds a single width from start to finish. Satoshi, a sans with a soaring x-height, supplies the contrast.
gen-gf-baumans-switzer: Wrench-wide c, uniform strokes: Baumans comes on strong. Baumans makes its mark as the display voice, whereas Switzer, a sans of wire-like letterforms and a tall waist line, handles the quieter body work.
gen-gf-baumans-work-sans: Baumans is distinctive from the first glance: a wide crescent c, uniform strokes. Work Sans, a contemporary sans with its mean line set high, rises well past Baumans in lowercase height, and that gap defines the pair.
gen-gf-bellota-archivo: Laser-cut and distinctive, Bellota hangs the ends of its s far from the spine, every stroke traced at one stylus width. Give Archivo, an editorial sans with a commanding x-height, a slightly smaller size.
gen-gf-bellota-fs-asap: Sharp, commanding lines that hold their width through every turn: that is Bellota. Asap, a sans with open-arc c forms and a body height near the capitals, does the quiet reading work while Bellota draws the eye.
